Definition: from G473 and G591; to requite (good or evil):--recompense, render, repay.
BiblicalUsage: To repay, to recompense, to give back what is owed, good or evil. God will repay tribulation to those who trouble His people, no man can first give to God and be repaid, vengeance belongs to the Lord, and the good who cannot repay you now will be repaid at the resurrection of the just. The word covers both sides of the same coin: God's repayment to the wicked and His reward to the faithful.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God keeps the accounts, and that is both my warning and my comfort: vengeance is His, not mine, and the kindness no one repaid will be repaid at the resurrection. I hold that no good deed is ever lost and no wrong ever forgotten, because the Lord repays, in His time and in His way.
